analysis.title: Asian Carnage: A Recap Of The Shocking Moves Across The Continent
key_insights: Asian equities sold off sharply on Oct 15, 2026. Notional traded on the Goldman Asia desk was up 58% vs its previous 20-day average. The desk was 1.2x better to sell overall and net to sell in every market except Australia (1.4x better to buy).

By sector, desk flow was most active in Information Technology (1.4x better to sell), Industrials (1.1x better to sell) and Materials (1.1x better to sell). Consumer Discretionary and Consumer Staples were flat.

The desk saw no panic in the flow, with a possible exception in Korea. Selling was steady through the whole session rather than concentrated in the morning, and traders who expected a bounce kept returning to sell. Defensive sectors were also sold, to a lesser extent.

Korea fell 7.6%, the largest selloff since July 28, 2026. Circuit breakers triggered on both KOSPI and KOSDAQ for the first time since July 29. Semiconductors closed down 12%, and foreigners sold $3.6bn.

SK Hynix saw foreign net selling of $830m, extending foreign selling to 15 consecutive sessions. Retail and local institutional buying did not offset it. Samsung also saw foreign net selling of roughly $1.1bn on a multi-day streak, with local institutions (+$375m) buying the dip.
The Kospi is down exactly 20%. This comes one week after the desk warned that Korean mega-buybacks are ending.

Japan's Nikkei fell 4.90%, its worst day since March 9. The Goldman Japan semiconductor basket (GSXAJSEM) fell 11.6%, its third-largest drawdown since creation. Kioxia closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time in its history.
Goldman's Japan flows were up 85% vs the month-to-date average and 40% above the year-to-date average. The desk saw more non-traditional flow, again with no panic.

Taiwan's TWSE fell 3.4% on the largest foreign institutional net selling day in history, about $9.3bn. Turnover was among the highest of the past year, exceeded only by the 6/26 session, which was also a 3.6% decline.
TSMC reported earnings after the close, described as mostly in line and likely not enough to turn sentiment positive.

Hong Kong was relatively stable, with the HSI down 1.03%. Every thematic sector closed lower, led by China Optical Network (-5.08%), China Data Centers (-4.76%) and China AI Value (-3.72%). Southbound investors net sold $647m, the largest net selling in over two weeks, and the Goldman desk saw selling in all sectors with notional traded up 38% vs its 3-week average.
earnings_insights: TSMC reported earnings after the close on Oct 15, 2026. The desk described them as mostly in line and likely not enough to turn sentiment positive. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
risk_factors: Continued foreign selling in Korean memory and chip names (SK Hynix foreign selling streak of 15 sessions)
End of Korean corporate buybacks, which had supported the Kospi
Momentum and memory/chip trade unwinding across North Asia, with Japanese semiconductors and Kioxia breaking technical levels
Broad selling that includes defensive sectors, suggesting de-risking beyond tech
